f97755c4.r: AI is exceptionally good at data synthesis, report writing, and presentation building, though humans must still verify the strategic intent.

Now, AI-powered sensors and computer vision monitor packaging lines and storage conditions in real-time, automatically flagging deviations and generating compliance documentation before you even step onto the floor. This automation doesn't replace you; it grants you the 'superpowers' needed to tackle the most complex threats to the food chain.

With the administrative burden lifted, you now focus on high-stakes investigations and proactive prevention. You use AI to analyze complex chemical signatures to detect sophisticated food fraud and predict bacterial outbreaks before they occur. Your work week is no longer defined by routine checklists, but by your ability to interpret AI-driven insights, lead advanced staff training simulations, and design robust safety programs that adapt to global supply chain shifts. You have become the ultimate arbiter of trust in the food system.
